title: Breaking Down the Israel–Iran Conflict: What We Know So Far - Day 9
byline: This guide answers the most important questions about the Israel Iran war that is unfolding right now. The United States and Israel have launched major military strikes on Iran and Iran has responded with missile attacks across the region. This is one of the most serious escalations in the Middle East in years.

title: CEB no more: Major power sector restructuring begins
byline: In a historic shake-up of Sri Lanka’s power sector, the Ceylon Electricity Board (CEB) has been officially dissolved and replaced with six separate state-owned companies from midnight yesterday, marking the beginning of a major restructuring of the country’s electricity industry.

title: Sri Lanka better equipped than before to absorb oil shocks: CB Governor
byline: Sri Lanka is better equipped than during its 2022 financial crisis to absorb shocks from rising oil prices, Central Bank Governor Dr. Nandalal Weerasinghe said, citing a strong US$ 7 billion foreign reserve buffer and low inflation as critical safeguards.

title: Private sector credit grows 26.3% in January despite seasonal slowdown
byline: ​Credit to the private sector by licensed commercial banks continued unabated through January 2026 at a faster pace from a year earlier, although the amount of loans granted fell sharply from the levels seen in December 2025 due to seasonal effects.

title: Early March tourist arrivals dip 25% as Middle East conflict disrupts vital transit hubs
byline: ​Sri Lanka’s tourism sector is navigating a complex landscape in early March 2026, grappling with a slowdown in arrivals following two consecutive record-breaking months.

title: Shippers’ Council warns of supply chain hits from Middle Eastern shipping disruptions
byline: The Sri Lanka Shippers’ Council has raised concerns over the mounting disruptions to global shipping and supply chains driven by the ongoing geopolitical tensions in the Middle East.

title: February worker remittances robust at US$ 729mn
byline: ​Sri Lankan remittances remained robust in February 2026, totalling US$ 729.0 million, up from US$ 548.1 million a year earlier, though slightly below January’s US$ 751.1 million.

title: Security of Sri Lankans in the northern region of Israel ensured: Ambassador
byline: Steps have been taken to ensure the safety of Sri Lankans residing in Northern Israel, Sri Lankan Ambassador in Israel said yesterday.

title: Oil barrels and debris washed ashore on Sri Lanka’s southern coast after IRIS Dena attack
byline: Several oil barrels and suspicious debris have washed ashore along Sri Lanka’s southern coastline a few days after the Iranian frigate IRIS Dena was torpedoed and sunk by the United States Navy submarine in seas off the coast of Galle.

title: Sri Lanka braces for food, energy supply shocks amid widening Middle East conflict
byline: Amid the widening conflict in the Middle East, the Sri Lankan government is bracing for possible disruptions to energy and essential food supplies and potential price spikes in the months ahead, though there is no immediate major threat.

title: Love for motherland must reflect respect for mothers: Namal
byline: Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) National Organiser and MP Namal Rajapaksa said a society that fails to respect mothers and women cannot build genuine love and respect for the motherland.

title: Aravinda bats for further reduction in lending rates
byline: Cricketer turned investor-cum-entrepreneur Aravinda de Silva last week made a compelling case for a further reduction in lending rates whilst reiterating his strong belief in Sri Lanka’s potential to do better.

title: Higher standard of English now required to settle in the UK
byline: Migrants will need to speak English to a higher standard if they wish to stay permanently in the UK, under landmark reforms introduced tomorrow.

title: 104 killed in US attack on Iranian warship off Sri Lanka, Iran’s army says
byline: Iran’s army said Sunday that 104 crew members of the Iranian warship IRIS Dena were killed and 32 others injured in a US attack last week, Anadolu reports.

title: Govt. assures national security amid global tensions
byline: Public Security Minister Ananda Wijepala said Sri Lanka is maintaining a neutral and non-aligned policy in line with international conventions amid rising tensions between Iran, the United States and Israel, while assuring that national security remains a top priority.

title: Oil soars past $100 a barrel as US-Israel war on Iran rages
byline: Oil prices have surged past $100 a barrel amid the fallout of the United States and Israel’s war on Iran.

title: Iran names Mojtaba Khamenei as new supreme leader
byline: Iran has named Mojtaba Khamenei as its new supreme leader, just over a week after the assassination of his father, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, in joint United States-Israeli strikes that have plunged the entire region into a sprawling war.

title: Possible fuel shortage looms if urgent steps not taken, Union warns
byline: Concerns are mounting in Sri Lanka over a potential fuel shortage after April, despite government assurances of adequate reserves. Ananda Palitha, Convener of the Samagi Joint Trade Union Alliance, said that recent remarks by Trade Minister Wasantha Samarasinghe regarding fuel sufficiency have instead fueled public anxiety.

title: How is Sri Lanka responding to the Israel–Iran conflict: Day 9
byline: As tensions escalate between Israel and Iran, Sri Lanka has taken a series of diplomatic, aviation and precautionary measures to manage potential fallout and safeguard its citizens. Here is how Sri Lanka is responding.

title: Hot weather may trigger skin problems, dehydration in children
byline: Health officials have warned that the prevailing hot weather conditions in the country could lead to an increase in skin problems and dehydration among children.

title: IMF’s Georgieva warns Middle East conflict could push global inflation higher
byline: IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva ​on Monday warned ‌of inflation risks from the Middle East conflict, ​saying a 10% ​increase in oil prices, ⁠if persistent through ​most of the year, ​would result in a 40-basis-point increase in global inflation.

title: G7 finance ministers to discuss joint oil reserve release - report
byline: G7 finance ministers will hold an emergency meeting on Monday to discuss a possible joint release of petroleum from reserves coordinated by the International Energy Agency, as oil prices surge following the conflict in the Gulf, according to the Financial Times.

title: PM Harini leaves for Philippines
byline: Prime Minister Dr. Harini Amarasuriya left for Manila, Philippines, at midnight yesterday (08) on an official visit at the invitation of the Asian Development Bank (ADB) to participate in events marking International Women’s Day.

title: Middle East attacks: Four injured Sri Lankans discharged
byline: The four Sri Lankans who were injured in recent attacks in the Middle East have been discharged from the hospital and are recovering, said Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs Arun Hemachandra.

title: U.S. Pacific Command recognizes Sri Lanka acted according to international law
byline: The US Indo-Pacific Command has recognized that Sri Lanka provided life-saving support to survivors of the Iranian warship IRIS Dena in accordance with the Law of Armed Conflict or the International Humanitarian Law.

title: SriLankan Airlines operates special charter flight from Colombo to Rome
byline: SriLankan Airlines has operated a special charter flight from Colombo to Rome today to repatriate a group of citizens, following a request from the Italian Embassy, informed sources said.

title: SriLankan Airlines to resume flights to Riyadh and Dubai
byline: SriLankan Airlines has announced that it will resume its flight operations to Riyadh and Dubai following a temporary disruption caused by the situation in the Middle East.

title: Australians turn to VPNs after adult website blocked under new age laws
byline: Virtual private network apps have skyrocketed up the app charts in Australia after a number of adult sites began blocking Australian users in compliance with new online safety codes in effect from Monday.

title: Teen arrested in Nawagattegama over viral reckless riding video
byline: A 19-year-old youth was arrested by police in Nawagattegama after a video showing reckless motorcycle riding went viral on social media, police said.

title: Nedungamuwe Raja’s preserved body to go on public display from March 11
byline: The preserved body of the famed elephant Nedungamuwe Raja will be opened for public viewing from March 11 and could remain intact for nearly 500 years if properly maintained, officials said.

title: Sajin Vass arrested
byline: Former Member of Parliament Sajin Vass Gunawardena has been arrested by officers of the Bribery Commission on charges of amassing illegal assets worth Rs. 243.8 million.

title: Bangladesh orders all universities closed to save electricity
byline: Bangladesh will close all universities from Monday, bringing forward the Eid al-Fitr holidays as part of emergency measures to conserve ​electricity and fuel amid a worsening energy crisis linked to ‌the conflict in the Middle East.

title: South Korea to impose fuel price cap to shield economy from energy shock
byline: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung said on Monday that authorities would cap ‌domestic fuel prices for the first time in nearly 30 years to contain a spike in prices after the conflict in the Middle East sent global crude prices sharply higher.

title: Cyclone Ditwah shows growing climate-driven disaster risks for Sri Lanka: Report
byline: Sri Lanka’s recent experience with Cyclone Ditwah highlights how extreme weather events linked to climate change are increasingly shaping the country’s disaster risks, according to a new report by Greenpeace South Asia.

title: G7 finance ministers to discuss joint oil reserve release - report
byline: G7 finance ministers will hold an emergency meeting on Monday to discuss a possible joint release of petroleum from reserves coordinated by the International Energy Agency, as oil prices surge following the conflict in the Gulf, according to the Financial Times.

title: Over 2,000 CEB employees apply for VRS
byline: Head of the CEB Transformation Task Force, Pubudu Niroshan Hedigalla said today that a total of 2,153 employees of the Ceylon Electricity Board (CEB) have applied for the Voluntary Retirement Scheme (VRS).

title: EDL takes over CEB’s electricity distribution under power reforms
byline: Electricity Distribution Lanka (Private) Limited (EDL) has officially taken over electricity distribution responsibilities previously handled by the Ceylon Electricity Board (CEB), as part of the power sector reforms introduced through the Electricity Act No. 36 of 2024.

title: Sajin Vass Gunawardena remanded
byline: Former Parliamentarian Sajin Vass Gunawardena, who was arrested by the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption over allegations of illegally acquiring assets worth Rs. 243.8 million, was today remanded till March 24 by Colombo Chief Magistrate Asanga S. Bodaragama.

title: CEB  restructuring should have been done with utmost care: Sajith
byline: The restructuring of the Ceylon Electricity Board (CEB) should have been done with utmost diligence, Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa said today.

title: Gary Kirsten appointed Sri Lanka men’s head coach
byline: Gary Kirsten has been appointed as the new head coach of the Sri Lanka national men’s cricket team, Sri Lanka Cricket said. His appointment will take effect from April 15, 2026.

title: New Secretary appointed to Ministry of Plantation, Community Infrastructure
byline: Gunadasa Samarasinghe has been appointed as the new Secretary to the Ministry of Plantation and Community Infrastructure, President’s Media Division (PMD)said.

title: Global Tensions Trigger Sharp Sell-Off; CSE Ends Deep in the Red
byline: The Colombo market suffered a sharp decline on 09th March 2026, as escalating conflict in the Middle East sparked fears of a global fuel supply shock, prompting panic selling across the CSE. The ASPI plunged 818 points intraday, and despite a modest recovery, closed 797 points lower, reflecting widespread caution among investors.

title: Putin congratulates new supreme leader
byline: Russian President Vladimir Putin congratulates Mojtaba Khamenei on his appointment as Iran’s new leader, the Kremlin says.

title: Electricity trade unions launch strike over job security concerns
byline: Twenty-five electricity trade unions have launched strike duties from 3 p.m. today, demanding the signing of a collective agreement and assurances on employee rights in the aftermath of the Ceylon Electricity Board (CEB) restructuring.

title: China says it opposes any targeting of new Iran leader
byline: China said on March 9 that Iran’s decision to name Mr Mojtaba Khamenei as its new supreme leader following the killing of his father was a domestic matter, and it opposed any attempt to target him.

title: Fuel prices increased from tonight
byline: The Ceylon Petroleum Corporation (CPC) has announced a revision of fuel retail prices with effect from tonight (09).

title: Civil Aviation Authority refutes social media posts on charter flight to Rome
byline: Refuting social media reports that SriLankan Airlines flight UL 1213 departed to bring a Government Minister back to the country, the Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) said today the Minister mentioned in these reports had already returned to Sri Lanka several days ago.
